# openprovider_dns_zone (Resource)

Manages a DNS zone. A zone holds the records that `openprovider_dns_record` manages. A change of any argument replaces the zone, and with it all of its records.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "openprovider_dns_zone" "example" {
  zone_name = "example.com"

  # Set to true to let `terraform destroy` delete the zone and all of its
  # records at OpenProvider. By default the zone is only forgotten.
  allow_deletion = false
}

resource "openprovider_dns_record" "www" {
  zone_name = openprovider_dns_zone.example.zone_name
  name      = "www"
  type      = "A"
  value     = "192.0.2.1"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `zone_name` (String) The name of the zone, for example `example.com`.

### Optional

- `allow_deletion` (Boolean) Enable deletion of this zone. When false (default), the zone is removed from Terraform state but preserved in OpenProvider, as for `openprovider_dns_record`. Set to true to permit actual deletion, which also deletes all records of the zone.
- `master_ip` (String) The IP address of the master name server. Only for a zone of the type `slave`.
- `provider_name` (String) The DNS provider that hosts the zone. If it is not set, OpenProvider uses its default (`openprovider`).
- `secured` (Boolean) Whether the zone is signed with DNSSEC. If it is not set, OpenProvider decides.
- `template_name` (String) The name of a DNS template (see `openprovider_dns_template`) whose records the new zone starts with. Only used when the zone is created.
- `type` (String) The type of the zone: `master` (default) or `slave`.

### Read-Only

- `creation_date` (String) The date and time when the zone was created.
- `extension` (String) The extension of the zone (`com` in `example.com`).
- `id` (String) The zone name.
- `modification_date` (String) The date and time when the zone was last modified.
- `name` (String) The name part of the zone (`example` in `example.com`).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# A zone is imported by its name.
terraform import openprovider_dns_zone.example example.com
```
